html:
Preparing to Track the Campaign

The last chapter helped establish the mechanism for planning the inbound marketing campaigns.  It took the components of the marketing matrix, that is, the vertical target segments, the bucketed serialized messages, and the appropriate social media channels, and combined them into a rolling editorial calendar that helped plan the content strategy. In all, your campaign should resemble the graphic flow below, as previously discussed.

Conventional Goal Funnel with Awareness, Acquisition, and Retention components

 

Targeting the Market defines the focus of your efforts. The company or individual should never have to worry about what or how the content should be developed and delivered. 

The social media channels have been selected for consumer acquisition.  The email campaign has been designed on the 2x2x2 rule (Chapter 5), and content has been planned within the editorial calendar framework.  Blog content is ready to be composed and posted on the website, scheduled appropriately based on the editorial calendar.  And finally, in this chapter, calls-to-action will be strategically placed on the website relative to goals that the company or individual has established.

Now, all that is left before launching the campaign is determining what metrics the company or individual will track to monitor its success.  It is now time to create a tracking system that will audit the campaign progress and provide marketing managers timely feedback to continue on the message or determine an alternative approach should the campaign fall short of the desired goals. 

Measure Results: Use analytics to track your goal funnel conversions.

  • Social Media Magnet Analytics Snapshot
  • Google Analytics
  • Facebook Insights
  • Instagram Insights
  • Twitter Analytics
  • MailChimp Analytics
  • Aggregators: SimplyMeasured.com, SocialScore, etc.

Tweak the Campaign

  • If it’s not working, or producing the desired results, tweak the campaign.
  • Research better verticals, better buckets, or different channels.
title: 7.1 Preparing to Track the Campaign

html:
Platform Insights for Social Acquisition

In order to successfully track the inbound campaign, several different measurements will be assembled from the various components of the campaign design. For example, within the consumer acquisition module of the campaign, platform insights from the various social media channels and/or social media management tools will be used to determine the successful acquisition of new readers/followers to your social media.  Here, Facebook Insights is a primary example of this auditing process (seen below).

Platform Insights - Facebook

We will talk more about specific measurements and their meanings later in Chapter 12. Still, at this stage in the pre-launch process, marketers should expect to be watching various analytics in the launching phases of the campaign.  Insights from Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, etc., will provide valuable information into the types and styles of messages resonating with the consumer audience. In addition, determination about image style, video style, permalink inclusion, technical versus funny, and other important design clues will be gleaned through this process. 

Acquiring Followers regardless of the Social Media Channel is essential. While not as powerful as garnering Email Addresses, it is the next best thing. These followers become the foundation for all of your future content campaigns, even your paid advertising campaigns. Make sure you are growing your audience by growing your followers. This is one area where we recommend adding a paid campaign early on to attract and grow your followers. It will also have a contribution to increasing your organic reach as well.

Platform Insights - Facebook Likes

The regular monitoring of social media channels will help hone in the message style to create a consistent brand persona.  Messages that are off-brand and underperforming will begin to become identifiable through the repeated auditing of these channels. 

Platform Insights - Facebook Reach over 15,667*

*Note the impact of the Paid Likes Campaign on Overal Reach. The Paid Likes Campaign opened up and expanded the Campaign Reach for all Posts.

While this may take a few weeks to a few months to determine, social media metrics will help to identify the correct serialized messages that will reliably produce increased awareness and, hopefully, click-throughs to the website. But, again, remember, this is an acquisition strategy.  The idea of acquiring new readers/customers/followers is predicated on using creative content to “pull” them into the website and then complete an action or goal on site. 

While building audience awareness at each social media channel is important (i.e., growing your followers). It provides you little value if you are not converting them on your website through a goal funnel.  You MUST have a goal for them to complete converting them into email subscribers. Build your Audience first, then customers. This will turn them into paying customers for your product or service, which is the ultimate goal, but more importantly, Retain them and turn them into Advocates.

Platform Insights Facebook Post Engagement by Post*

Note: Post Reach and Engagement by Post metrics over time. Watch both High and Low performing Posts to continue to improve Post Engagement driving drive traffic to your Website.

Once your social media starts funneling readers to your website, this is where Google Analytics will take over.  No website should function without Google Analytics plugged in on the backside to monitor how your traffic is coming into the website, what they are doing while they are there, and how and where they are leaving the website.  Google will also help you track goal funnel conversions on site.
title: 7.2 Platform Insights for Social Acquisition

html:
Google Analytics: Traffic Coming into the Website

Overall Website Traffic is measured at Google Analytics. In addition, the top-level Google Analytics Audience Overview report shows traffic for the period and may compare it to previous periods and years.

Audience Overview

To monitor incoming traffic to your website and to know where they came from, the acquisition tab in the left-hand sidebar will show traffic from each channel, and each is performing along with the quality of the traffic based on Users, Sessions, Bounce Rate, Time on Site, Pages Visited, etc.

Referral Traffic - All Channels

In the example above, readers enter in four ways: Direct, Organic Search, Social, or Referral.  Direct channels represent those who type the specific name of the website into their web browser’s search bar, e.g., www.socialmediamagnetpro.com.  Direct is usually a function of top-of-mind awareness about a particular site.  When individuals type in a URL link directly into the search bar, they are usually very familiar with the site and frequently use it. Email traffic is often reported in the Direct channel  Organic Search channels to include individuals who entered search criteria into a major search engine like Google, Bing, or Yahoo! and clicked on the website through the search engine.  Social channels refer to people entering indirectly from a social media channel through a permalink (i.e., a link to an individual blog post) placed within the social post.  Permalinks are strategically used to funnel readers into the website using a “hook” in the social media post to draw people into wanting more information. Below is a deeper dive providing a snapshot of how each Social Channel is performing.

Social Referrals by Channel

Many times, questions posed to the reader are used as a hook to ask readers to click the link to find out the answer to the question or more about the topic at hand.  Giving too much away in the social post will prevent readers from clicking through to the website.  There is a fine balance here between hook content and click-through that can be learned over time. 

Finally, referral channels include websites that have posted a company’s or individual’s content on their page and created a backlink (an incoming hyperlink from one web page to another website) to another company’s or individual’s page, which a person clicked on and was directed to the company or individual website.

Next, it is important to know how well the social channels work to bring individuals into the website.  By clicking directly on “Social” within the Acquisition – Overview tab in the left-hand sidebar of the Google Analytics Dashboard, a company or individual can determine how many users are coming to the website from the various operational social media channels.  In the example below, the analyst can determine that during the last 28 days, 183 new visitors to the website have come via Facebook, with only a handful from Yelp, LinkedIn, Twitter, and Instagram.  If these last four channels are strategically viable, meaning that there are active content posts to these channels, a change of focus would be needed to increase traffic from these social platforms.  However, it’s more likely that these channels are not being utilized like Facebook. This company is beginning to test other social channels now that Facebook has become a primary social channel for them.

Website Analytics Dashboard

The Social Media Magnet Pro provides plugin software to consolidate your Analytics into a single Dashboard and weekly snapshot on your key metrics of Awareness, Acquisition, and Retention. The above image is what the Dashboard looks like on your WordPress Website, and we also provide a view by Week from your Member Dashboard - see screenshot example further below.

Website Analytics Dashboard - Weekly Analytics

This tab, Weekly Analytics, generates Posts automatically on your website that show Analtycis aggregated from your Google Analytics, pulling together the top KIPs by week and combining the stats from your MailChimp email account into a single report. Each week our software goes out and gathers all your actual Analytics and presents it to you on your website, to review and be gathered to www.socialmediamagnetpro.com to rank your performance. Clicking on any single Week will show the Analytics To-Date. NOTE: We cumulate your Analytics, adding each new week to the previous combined Weeks. You should see ALL of your metrics growing weekly overtime. If this is flattering, you have stopped growing. The Subscribers number is the actual Active Subscribers currently. It will grow as you ad New and decline as people Opt-out.

Website Analytics Dashboard - Weekly Analytics - Week Report

These Week reports are imported into our software at the Social Media Magent Pro www.socialmediamagentpro.com and may be accessed via your Dashboard Link > Member Analytics. Your Campaign will not begin reporting and results until you enter your Live Campaign Start Date. We will discuss and review in the Assignment setting up the Software and your campaign later.

SMMPro Member Analytics Live Campaign

Each week, your campaign results will be added to the previous results to give you a cumulative report of your campaign results. We show you have your campaign is progressing for the KPIs for each category grouped by Awareness, Acquisition, and Retention, reporting the changes each week. This should look familiar to the Conventional Goal Funnel image discussed in section 7.1 Preparing to Track the Campaign. But now, we see the actual numbers and their impact.

SMMPro Member Analytics Live Campaign with Infinity Loop

You should begin to get the feel of your traffic and whether you are on track or not. The growth or decline will push you to the left or the right. Remember, growth of New without the Retention of Existing will push you in one direction or another, eventually causing issues and no balanced growth.

SMMPro Member Analytics Live Campaign with Infinity Loop and Social Media Magnet

As you can see, looking at the data and analytics is one thing; being able to turn it into INFORMATION and know what it means and how it affects your Live Campaign is an acquired skill that will guide you to continuous growth. Therefore, you must learn how to look through the data through the lens of the Social Media Magent to know the rhythm and flow of your audience and your messaging.

Next, we will break down the analytic categories into a closer view by each Awareness, Acquisition, and Retention.

SMMPro Member Analytics Live Campaign Awareness

Users, New Users, Sessions, and Pageviews provide the top traffic levels within the website, just as we discussed regarding Google Analytics. This report shows you how they are performing relative to each other and cumulative week over week. If you see a softening or even upticks in the report week over week, you can drill into this data at your Google Analytics account to peek under the hood and see what is happening. The purpose of this dashboard is to provide a higher-level view and whether your Socia Media Magent is performing or not and get a feel for the trends week to week.
title: 7.3 Google Analytics: Traffic Coming into the Website

html:
Google Analytics: Traffic Within and Leaving the Website

Once individuals have found their way into the website, then Google Analytics will help determine several important factors, including how many users and pageviews are occurring on-site, which webpages are most viewed, what is the behavioral flow of an individual from one webpage to another, and finally, are individuals moving through the goal funnel to complete the call-to-action.

This traffic source is measured in the SMMPro Member Analytics Live Campaign presented in the Acquisition section. This shows you where your traffic came from; Direct, Social Organic, and Referrals, as we have previously discussed. As you can see below, they must work together.

SMMPro Member Analytics Live Campaign Acquisition

First, let’s address the question of how many. To explore how many users, new users, sessions, and pageviews are occurring at the website, click the Audience – Overview tab in the left-hand sidebar of your Google Analytics Dashboard, as demonstrated below.  In this example, over the last 28 days, there have been 898 Users to the website, of which 775 of those users were new to the site. In addition, there were 1230 Sessions, where a single session can contain multiple page views, events, social interactions, etc.  In other words, one Session is the full length of time that an individual spends with the website before clicking out of the website and on to something else.  Here, the average session duration, or the length of time of one session, was 2 minutes and 33 seconds.  Average session durations are usually between 2-3 minutes but can vary by industry.  In this case, 2:33 is a typical expectation.  Lastly, this data shows that there have been 2,514 Pageviews over this time period, or the viewing of anyone single page on-site, for an average of 2.04 pages per session.  This specific data suggests that the company or individual here had only 2 minutes and 33 seconds, and only two web pages, to convey the marketing message and convince the average reader to act on the content.  This kind of puts the importance of concise, on-brand, serialized messages into perspective, doesn’t it?

 

Next, as seen in the example below, the Behavioral Overview tab within Google Analytics will identify how many pageviews the company or individual has had within a specific time frame.  This example included the last 28 days, from August 1 to August 28.  Additionally, it listed the top viewed pages, with the homepage listed as the most viewed at 22.35% of the total views over the last month.  Note that while this page in this example is listed as the most viewed, all other pages together make up 77.65% of the pages.  Note: If the content acquisition strategy is working properly, the homepage will not be the page most individuals enter the website on.  This is a common misperception.  In fact, if done properly, the homepage should not and will not be the most viewed page of content. Instead, as a company or individual develops content leadership (as explained in the last chapter), then their defined content pages, often called blog pages or article pages, will become the most viewed web pages.  As you can see in the example above, the fourth most viewed page has an “/articles/” tag to it, which means for this company, this is a specific blog article that is moving up the most viewed list, being posted only a week ago within this month’s cycle of content.

Moving on to the specific flow of website visitors, let’s continue exploring their behavior.  Clicking the tab labeled “Behavior Flow” below the Behavioral Overview tab will demonstrate how individuals are moving from webpage to webpage and where they leave the page altogether.  In the example below, the webpage with the highest number of entries is the main homepage (denoted by “ / ”) at 429 views over the last month.  If you hover over this green box for the homepage (demonstrated in the bottom right-hand corner of the graphic below), you will see that of these 429 visitors, 189 moved on to another page in the website, where 240 visitors are “drop-offs,” meaning they exited the website.  The next column demonstrates that viewers moved mainly to “/meet-our-team/” first and then on to the “/complete list of services/” next from the homepage.  Following the gray path lines will give each analyst an understanding of how traffic moves through the website.  Hovering over each box will also provide data on where each viewer exits the website altogether.

Lastly, if an analyst wants to drill down into the content and see exactly how well each page is doing, then they can click on the “Site Content” tab under the Behavior tab.  For example, if they wanted to know what kind of blog articles are getting the most views, then clicking on articles (or blog, depending on your categorical tag for these type of website posts) one would be able to determine what type of blogs are most popular on the site.  In the example below, “patient stories” are getting the most views.  Drilling down one more level by clicking on “/articles/” would tell which type of blog has been the most viewed on site.  Drilling down even one more level by clicking on “/patient stories/” would tell which personal story blog has been most popular over the last 30 days.
title: 7.4 Google Analytics: Traffic Within and Leaving the Website

html:
Google Analytics: Traffic Moving through the Goal Funnel

Google Analytics will also help you keep track of conversions through the goal funnel.  There are many different uses for goal funnels.  They can be used to track consumers through a shopping cart, for example, or through multiple pages of a signup form.  In their most basic form, they can be established to track any call-to-action on the website.  For instance, within the project practicum, they can track how many users on the website decide to sign up for a newsletter by visiting the sign-up page and, most importantly, how many follow through on that call-to-action.  They work by following the same user from submitting the form on the sign-up page to the Thank You page.  If the same user hits both pages in sequence, as established in the goal admin page, Google will record this action as a goal completion.  To set up a goal in Google Analytics, go to the admin screen denoted by the orange gear in the lower right-hand corner.  Clicking on the gear will open the Account – Property – View columns within the admin page. Next, click on the goals button under the view column, as pictured below.

There are various forms of goals that an analyst can track within Google.  For the sake of the discussion here, which is to track a sign-up to thank you goal funnel, the analyst will need to have both pages set up on the website first.  After copying the URLs of both the origination page (sign-up page) and the destination page (thank you page), one can set up the goal.  Once the analyst enters the goal screen (shown above), click on the red button entitled “+ New Goal.”

Upon entering the New Goal screen, the analyst will click the radio button labeled “custom” and then the submit button labeled “Continue.”  On the next screen, name the Goal whatever is appropriate (like Newsletter Sign-Up), click the “Destination” radio button, and click on the blue submit button entitled “Continue.”  On the next Goal Details screen, enter the destination page URL (thank you page) in the “Destination: Equals to:” the first box lined in blue in the picture below. Next, be sure to turn the funnel option ON from the OFF position, and in the second set of blue outlined boxes below, enter a “name” of the sign-up step and the origination page (sign-up page) into the “Screen/Page” fields.  Next, click the “Required?” toggle button next to the origination URL to “YES.” Before you hit save at the end of this process, your screen should resemble the picture below.  If so, then click the blue “Save” button at the bottom of the screen to complete the goal funnel creation process.

Now that the new goal funnel has been created, you can monitor your goal completion process with the Google Analytics Conversions tab located in the left-hand sidebar of the dashboard, as seen below.

SMMPro Member Analytics Live Campaign Goals

Goal Completions are reported on your Social Media Magnet Dashboard. We report All Goal Completions together are a single number. If you have more than one Goal set, you may use this to see how your goals are performing and use your Google Analytics to see how each individual Goal is performing. The Gaol Completions are reported cumulative adding the current week together with the previous total. You should see this continuing to grow. If your Goals flatten, you may need to evaluate your Call to Action and Posts to ensure your message has not strayed or your target market moved on.

Goal Funnel Traffic Moving Through to Completion

Google Analytics provides a Goal Funnel Visualization, Google Analytics > Conversions > Goals > Funnel Visualization. It provides excellent information about how your traffics is interacting with your Goals. You will see how many entered the funnel, how many moved through, and how many moved on to something else. This can provide insights into where you may have "constraints" in your Goal funnel or process. Sometimes it can be too many steps or something on the page. We have found sometimes changing the color of a button or location can contribute to improving completions.
title: 7.5 Google Analytics: Traffic Moving through the Goal Funnel

html:
Email Statistics for Consumer Retention

To conclude the campaign goal tracking process, especially as it is related to Live Campaign, it is important to monitor the email campaign to measure consumer retention among the most loyal of followers.  As has been said before, the hardest thing to acquire from any digital consumer is their email address. 

SMMPro Member Analytics Live Campaign Retention Email Stats

The Retention section of your Member Analytics shows the stats from your MailChimp Campaigns. We pull in the number of currently Active Subscribers (Opt-ins - Opt-Outs = Active Subscribers). We also accumulate week-over-week the Emails Sent, Opens, and Click-Throughs. These numbers should be growing as you continue to implement your campaign. If they stall or flatten, you need to take a harder look at your emails, content formation, message focus, and delivery. The top two reasons for declining results are 1) boring repetitive emails and/or 2) forgetting to send emails on a timely regular basis or altogether. If you are not sure, please revisit section 6.3 Designing the Editorial Calendar: Planning Content or section 5.3 Retention Post-Follower Email Campaigns.

Remember, if a reader is willing to give their email address to any company or individual, they find the content engaging enough to give up one of the most prized possessions in their email.  Additionally, they will be searching for continued evidence of the initial value because, at any point, the consumer can unsubscribe from any email list with just a couple of clicks due to compliance regulations.  For example, view the MailChimp report below.  Between Emails 10 and 11, the number of subscribers dropped by 63 subscribers, from 4,226 to 4,163.  Even though these individuals had previously subscribed to the weekly newsletter, for some reason, they unsubscribed from the mail list.  In these instances, most email listserve programs will allow the survey of these individuals to find out why they may be leaving for the analyst to know how to prevent this action in the future.

Additionally, email reports will also indicate two more important metrics, open rate percentage and click-throughs.  We have discussed these in previous chapters, but these two metrics provide the analyst a sense of whether or not the email title was enticing enough to cause the reader to open the email and then was the content engaging enough to cause the reader to click on the link, passing them through to more in-depth content.  This is why the Sender, Email Title, and Email Hook are so important.  Remember the 2x2x2 Email rule.  It takes 2 seconds for the reader to see who the email is from, 2 seconds for the reader to determine content from the subject line of the Email Title, and 2 seconds for them to determine interest from the Email Hook within the email body.  Consistent monitoring of a company or individual’s performance across the number of subscribers, open rate percentage, and click-through percentages will provide valuable information into the successful deployment of the consumer retention program, especially as companies compare across industry standards.  As can be seen in the MailChimp Report below, the example company has been running consistently above the industry average in open rates but has recently dipped below the average.  The second most recent email campaign shot back way above industry average, only to have the last one fall back to average.  The astute analyst should be looking at what Email #10 did differently and follow that plan of strategic execution for all following emails.

Google Analytics Email Traffic Coming into the Website

Google Analytics may report your Email Traffic to your website as a separate line item. However, it is often reported in the Direct Traffic line to the site. Your email traffic most influences this metric. Sometimes individuals may copy out the link, or the email tracking code may be blocked, causing the visit to be tracked a Direct Traffic. This traffic is one of the most beneficial in bringing traffic to your site, and it will also increase your Organic Search as the search engines reward you for the traffic at your site.  Make sure you are diligent and intentional in managing your email Analytics and results.
title: 7.6 Email Statistics for Consumer Retention

html:
Progress Reports

Metrics are vital to managerial decision-making

For any company or individual running an inbound marketing campaign, a consistent audit of these important metrics is vital to managerial decision-making.  Whether is about identifying your:

  • Brand Awareness: the total number of users, new users, sessions, or pageview on your website
  • Brand Acquisition: whether consumers are coming to your site due to email, social channels, organic search, or backlink referrals from other websites,
  • Brand Retention: tracking through goals how many users are completing your call-to-actions, subscribing to your email campaign, and opening/clicking through your actual emails.

In all of these instances, managerial decision-making should be based on analytics.  In future chapters, we will address the specific strategies related to these numbers. Still, it is important to realize that a company or individual must identify these metrics BEFORE the campaign to measure the impact of the content decisions.  Therefore, for the sake of Live Campaign, we have developed a progress report system that will be used during the entire campaign through our Social Media Magnet plugin.  This website analytics reporting mechanism should guide you about how the campaign is performing and how to adjust it appropriately.  Once the Live Campaign has begun, to access these weekly analytics, you will need to go to The Social Media Magnet Pro dashboard (not your WordPress dashboard) and click on the blue hyperlink called "Website Analytics."  Here you will find the following data to help you complete your three campaign progress reports.  Directions on these reports will be included in your Level 4 Assignments.  But for now, let's examine these reports.

Progress Reports: Raw Data

First, you will be provided the raw data for your website and MailChimp email campaigns weekly.  As you will see below, data will be collected across four items for each category of brand awareness, brand acquisition, and brand retention per week, from Sunday to Saturday.  The plugin will run a cron job (an automatic data pull) for each Live Campaign website every Sunday to report your weekly metrics.  Note: Metrics will be reported each week cumulatively, meaning that Week 3's report will include all of the data for Week 1, 2, and 3.  This cumulative reporting allows you to see how your website is growing each week.  Like an annuity investment, if you are performing the campaign correctly, then you should see compounded growth each week, as the previous week's blogs will still be helping increase traffic in future weeks (that is, if it is good content). The raw data will look like this:

Social Media Magnet Pro Member Analytics Raw Data

For awareness, the plugin will track how many users, new users, sessions, and pageviews you accumulated on your website each cumulative week.  The awareness measure is a function of how well your content is being perceived and how much traffic is flowing back to your website.  Good content is the impetus here.  If you have content with slugs that interest people, then they will click on your social links to come back to read the full blog article.  For acquisition, these numbers tell you where you are most successful in driving your traffic back to the site.  Specifically, these acquisition channels refer to:

  • Direct: Most of these website users are related to your email campaign.  Users are clicking on your email links and are pushed "directly" back to your website from the email link.  (Note: People who come in via the category of "Email" are typically users who have come in on a forwarded email from someone else.  Even though Google Analytics will demonstrate this category separately from Direct, we do NOT measure the "Email" category because it is not a user due to your primary action, again, since it was a forwarded email from someone else.)
  • Social: These users are clicking on links within social media platforms, most notably Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, LinkedIn, etc.  A deeper look into just the social channel will tell you which social channels are most productive in driving traffic to your site.
  • Organic Search: Users in this category find your website through search engines like Google, Bing, and Yahoo.  Search engine optimization and selection of the right keywords will help increase traffic in this category.
  • Referrals: Whenever another website shares your content and that users ethically create a backlink URL to your site, then these users who click on that backlink and end up at your site are called Referrals.

Next, the retention category measures the completion of the goals that have been set up on your website.  Specifically, you are required to set up a "Follow-Me" goal that will track the number of users who subscribe to your email campaign.  This "destination" goal tracks the number of users from your MailChimp sign-up form to your sign-up thank you page.  Building goal funnels in Google Analytics is an essential step in tracking the percentage of users completing your call-to-actions and how many abandon the goal funnel process.  If your abandonment rate is too high, there is often a problem with the goal funnel structure.  Lowering this rate will increase your goal completion numbers and increase your grade.  Also, within the retention category, the plugin will monitor your email campaign progress at MailChimp, recording your overall subscribers, email opens, and email click-throughs.  This is very important because the OVERALL goal of this entire organic process is to move users from the top of the goal funnel through to the bottom, which in this class is signing up email subscribers and retaining them as part of the Social Media Magnet theory.  Remember, your project overview looks like this:

 

You need to set up your goal funnels at this stage, as outlined in this chapter, to prepare for the campaign.  The other metrics will automatically track during the live campaign.

Progress Reports: Grades

Additionally, within the Website Metrics, you will also see below the raw data a set of score/grades associated with each of the single items (e.g., users, new users, sessions, etc.).  These grades are calculated from the mean and standard deviation for every single item across each Live Campaign program. You are competing with others, just like yourself. in your class. (Note: If you do not understand how mean and standard deviation are used to calculate a grade, we have a FAQ that will explain it to you.)  Like we have said before, this class is based on competition.  Just like the real world, you are competing against every other blogger in your domain, every other company in your product or service category, every other employee at your work for the promotion. Realistically, you are even competing against yourself to grow your social impact week over week, month over month, and year over year.  We have found that many people have trouble with the competition side of your Live Campaign, but we implore you to get used to this aspect.  As soon as you graduate, competition becomes the name of the game in a free-market society.  And just like the real world, your Live Campaign score/grade is based on how well you do on each of these metrics versus the other Live Campaign results.  These per item Score/Grades will appear like this:

Social Media Magnet Pro Member Analytics Grades

Along with each of the per item grades, you will also see a categorical grade, one each for Brand Awareness, Brand Acquisition, and Brand Retention.  These categorical grades are just averages for each of the four items in the category.  However, the revelation with these categorical grades is to realize how well (or poorly) you are doing in any one category.  The category with the lowest grade is one that you should probably focus on more diligently to raise your overall score/grade.  For example, in the demonstration below, this person is doing pretty well with their email campaign because the score/grade in the retention category is stronger at 87.06%.  But they are worse at driving traffic to their website because the awareness category score/grade is only 72.39%. 

Therefore, they should focus on creating stronger, more relevant content.  This poor content could be due to just overall weak content on their website blog, or it could be due to not blogging or posting enough in their social media channels.  A content audit could lead to why this content is failing and could potentially assist with the acquisition score/grade.  Better content should lead to more users being acquired from your social media platforms, which obviously would help your acquisition score/grade as well.

Social Media Magnet Pro Member Analytics Sub- Level Grades

Note: Remember, ALL (each item score/grade and categorical grade) are cumulative grades, starting Week 1 of the campaign through the current week's grades.  Therefore, the weekly grade, highlighted in purple, is a cumulative overall score/grade for your Live Campaign.  In reality, this IS your current overall Live Campaign score/grade.

You will be starting your Live Campaign soon.  Good luck, and please remember, your Live Campaign score/grade is HIGHLY CORRELATED with how hard you work on your campaign.  If you put in the time, then in most instances, you will receive the reward of a score/grade that is standard deviations above the mean.  But be sure to start at a sprint because, like the annuity metaphor, each week's metrics are compounding.  You want to get the full compounding effect over the entire Live Campaign, so start strong and keep running the race.  It's a marathon, but you can do it, and who knows, you might even enjoy it.
title: 7.7 Progress Reports

html:
SUMMARY AND REVIEW

CHAPTER SUMMARY

Chapter 7 was entirely about how to audit a campaign and make managerial decisions based on the analytics.  The chapter opened with a review of the course practicum, highlighting both the acquisition and retention components of the program.  It gave a brief overview of platform insights and the need for monitoring your social media channels for types and styles of messages that are and are not resonating with your target audience.  Next, an in-depth look at the exact metrics measured throughout this course was highlighted, as they identify individuals moving into, through, and exiting the website.  Google Analytics is used to identify the originating source of these patrons, and from what channel they entered.  Likewise, discussion identified processes for monitoring how many times each user comes, how long they stay, and where they exit the website after their session is complete.  Next, detailed instructions were given on how to set up a Google goal on-site and why that is important in conjunction with the ultimate goal of the project, signing up emails through a newsletter subscription process.  Finally, MailChimp reporting was discussed to wrap up the retention analytics for the entire campaign.  Now, at the end of this chapter, students should know exactly what is expected of them while monitoring the success of their live practicum.

KEY TERMS

backlink
direct channels
